title: Building an Adaptive Agentic Cybersecurity System with NVIDIA Nemotron | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA and CrowdStrike ran a joint evaluation in which an open Nemotron model stack (Nemotron 3 Ultra orchestrating, a post-trained Nemotron 3 Super writing detections) inside CrowdStrike's SafeMind agentic system beat a frontier-model system on detection generalization: 45% vs 29% of detections fired on eight unseen attacks, and three open detections qualified as 'gold' versus zero for the frontier system. CrowdStrike separately claims its Blue Solano defensive model is more accurate than the leading proprietary frontier model tested at 99% lower cost. The core argument is that harness specialization plus verifiable-reward post-training, not raw frontier scale, is what makes agentic security work.

insights.claim: CrowdStrike states that its Blue Solano defensive model is more accurate than the leading proprietary frontier model it tested while costing 99% less, based on CrowdStrike's own internal evaluations.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: A 99% cost delta at parity-or-better accuracy is the clearest signal yet that security-vendor inference spend migrates from frontier API tokens to owned, post-trained open weights — watch gross-margin expansion at security software vendors and pressure on frontier-model API revenue in vertical workloads.
insights.quote: CrowdStrike reports that its Blue Solano defensive model is more accurate than the leading proprietary frontier model tested, at 99% lower cost, in CrowdStrike internal evaluations.
insights.locator: NVIDIA and CrowdStrike evaluated an agentic

insights.claim: Open-weight models can be post-trained on proprietary domain data, deployed inside controlled environments with proprietary context, and tuned for cost and scale — a combination closed frontier APIs cannot offer in regulated or sensitive settings.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: The moat in vertical AI shifts from model access to proprietary telemetry plus post-training capability; favor firms with unique data exhaust (endpoint, transaction, clinical) over those reselling frontier API wrappers.
insights.quote: Open models such as Nemotron can be post-trained with domain data, deployed with proprietary context in controlled environments, and optimized for cost and scale.

insights.claim: The frontier system produced more backtest-passing detections (35 versus 11 for the open pipeline) yet produced zero gold-qualified detections, showing that raw output volume from a larger model can mask lower per-artifact quality.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: Benchmarks that count passing artifacts overstate frontier-model advantage; buyers evaluating agentic security tools should demand generalization and false-positive metrics, which is where smaller specialized stacks win.
insights.quote: The frontier system produced more backtest-passing detections, but the optimized Nemotron open-model pipeline yielded a higher share that generalized, averaged more detections per detection, and was the only system to produce gold detections.

insights.claim: Traditional red-team/blue-team security exercises are rate-limited by manual handoffs — attack execution, telemetry review, detection engineering, retest — which caps the number of attack variations an organization can ever evaluate.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: The bottleneck being labor, not tooling, means agentic automation attacks the largest cost line in security operations — a structurally large TAM for whoever automates detection engineering.
insights.quote: Each handoff takes time, limiting the number of iterations and attack variations teams can evaluate.
insights.locator: Turning offense and defense into a continuous learning loop

insights.claim: The evaluated system runs a four-stage closed loop — execute and capture, process and reconstruct, generate and validate, retest and adapt — in which the red agent receives the deployed detection context and searches for evasion paths until no viable route remains in the modeled environment.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: This is a reusable template for adversarial self-play in any domain with verifiable outcomes; expect the same loop pattern to appear in fraud, compliance, and QA products, each requiring sustained GPU capacity rather than one-off training runs.
insights.quote: The loop continues until no further viable path remains within the modeled environment.

insights.claim: Most current agentic security deployments remain anchored to existing alerts, predefined workflows, and known attack behaviors, meaning the genuinely hard problem — finding what defenses miss — is still largely unaddressed by shipping products.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: A market-segmentation cue: vendors marketing 'AI SOC' on top of existing alert pipelines are automating triage, not coverage; the coverage-gap category is comparatively open and is where differentiated value accrues.
insights.quote: The harder problem is identifying what defenses miss and turning those gaps into reliable coverage.
insights.locator: AI is changing the pace of cybersecurity.

insights.claim: NVIDIA supplied a sanitized natural-language specification of its own accelerated computing infrastructure, which an agent-assisted workflow translated into an isolated instrumented test environment reviewed by NVIDIA security experts for realism.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is using its own datacenter footprint as the reference threat model, which both hardens its supply chain and creates a template it can sell to every AI-factory operator standing up similar infrastructure.

insights.claim: Evaluation progress was measured from action traces and sensor telemetry against observable milestones rather than from the agent's own claims about what it accomplished.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: Ground-truth instrumentation is becoming the differentiator in agent evaluation; treat vendor agent-performance claims without external telemetry verification as unaudited.
insights.quote: The evaluation used attack paths and observable milestones to measure progress from action traces and sensor telemetry rather than the agent’s own claims.

insights.claim: The defensive harness added six specific mechanisms — a schema knowledge base, telemetry grounding, a specialized authoring model, artifact linting, detection replay, and independent judge review — each targeting a distinct failure mode of generic agent harnesses.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: Value in agentic products is concentrating in the harness and validation layer rather than the model; that layer is where vertical software vendors can build defensible IP against model-provider commoditization.
insights.locator: The defensive harness combined six mechanisms

insights.claim: Automated linting rejected detections tied to specific IP addresses, hosts, users, or subnets and returned guidance to rewrite around behavioral signals, encoding a rule that environment-specific strings produce detections that do not generalize.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: Deterministic guardrails, not larger models, are what convert plausible LLM output into deployable artifacts — a cheap, replicable pattern any enterprise AI buyer should ask vendors to demonstrate.
insights.quote: Failures returned guidance for rewriting the detection around behavioral signals instead of environment-specific strings.

insights.claim: Detection replay against captured telemetry caught candidate detections that appeared syntactically valid but failed to actually match the recorded attack, a failure class that static validation alone misses.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: Execution-based validation is the practical answer to LLM plausibility; markets for sandboxed execution and replay infrastructure grow alongside agentic deployments.
insights.quote: Detections that produced no match were rejected and returned for correction, catching candidates that appeared valid but failed to detect the recorded activity.

insights.claim: Separating a reasoning orchestrator from a bounded expert model keeps long-horizon workflow context distinct from the specialized authoring task, which the authors present as the reusable architecture rather than an implementation detail.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: Multi-model routing (large orchestrator plus small specialists) means inference demand fragments across model sizes rather than consolidating on one frontier model — bullish for flexible serving stacks and for mid-size model demand.
insights.quote: This separation kept workflow orchestration distinct from specialized detection authoring.

insights.claim: CrowdStrike's NL2LogScale expert was built from Nemotron 3 Super via continual pretraining on cybersecurity knowledge, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: A named, shipped vertical model derived from an open base is evidence the three-stage post-training recipe is now production practice, sustaining ongoing GPU training demand from software vendors, not just labs.

insights.claim: Fine-tuning used only 9,349 detection-generation and multistep repair examples spanning 59 programmatically generated error types, combining rephrasings from Nemotron 3 Super, real Falcon LogScale execution errors, and reviewed reasoning traces from Nemotron 3 Ultra.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: Under 10,000 curated examples was enough to build a competitive vertical expert — the data barrier to entry for domain models is far lower than assumed, which compresses the advantage of scale-only players.
insights.quote: Fine-tuning used 9,349 detection-generation and multistep repair examples spanning 59 programmatically generated error types.

insights.claim: The reward signal came from executing generated queries in Falcon LogScale and scoring the F1 overlap between events returned by the generated and reference queries, so the model was rewarded for matching results rather than for producing valid syntax.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: Verifiable-reward RL requires a real execution environment in the training loop, which raises infrastructure requirements per training run and favors vendors that own the execution substrate.
insights.quote: Valid generated and reference queries ran against the same synthetic logs, and the F1 overlap between their returned events supplied the reward.
insights.locator: For reinforcement learning, the training workflow

insights.claim: The RL loop gave invalid queries real engine errors and up to five repair attempts, assigning zero reward to unresolved attempts, which trains the model on realistic error-recovery rather than single-shot generation.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: Multi-turn repair capability is emerging as a distinct trainable skill and a likely axis of vendor differentiation in agentic tooling.
insights.quote: Invalid queries received real engine errors and up to five repair attempts, with unresolved attempts receiving zero reward.
insights.locator: For reinforcement learning, the training workflow

insights.claim: The full training path used NVIDIA NeMo Gym for query validation and execution and NVIDIA NeMo RL with group relative policy optimization for model updates, positioning NeMo as the integrated post-training stack alongside the Nemotron weights.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is bundling open weights with a software stack that pulls through GPU consumption at both training and inference — the software layer is the lock-in mechanism, not the model license.
insights.locator: For reinforcement learning, the workflow used NeMo Gym

themes.theme: Measured results: backtest to live fire

insights.claim: Nemotron 3 Ultra on a default agent harness produced detections that caught the recorded attack only 16.5% of the time on average across eight independently seeded sessions.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: The out-of-the-box baseline is weak enough that any 'just point an LLM at it' security product should be assumed near-unusable without a validation harness.
insights.quote: With Nemotron 3 Ultra and the default harness, an average of 16.5% of generated detections detected the recorded attack across eight independently seeded sessions.

insights.claim: Adding the tuned harness, the customized Nemotron 3 Super, domain context, tools, and validation raised the mean backtest detection rate to 41.9% across six sessions — a 2.5x improvement over the same orchestrator on a default harness.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: A 2.5x gain from engineering around a fixed orchestrator quantifies how much headroom sits outside model weights — capex for harness engineering may beat capex for bigger models.
insights.quote: Retaining Ultra while adding the tuned harness, customized Nemotron 3 Super, domain context, tools, and validation raised the mean to 41.9% across six sessions, a 2.5x improvement.

insights.claim: In live-fire testing against eight unseen attacks, 5 of 11 open-pipeline detections (45%) fired versus 10 of 35 frontier detections (29%), and the open pipeline averaged 2.6 detections per detection versus 1.1 for the frontier system.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: Generalization, not backtest pass rate, is the metric that predicts production value; the 45%-vs-29% gap is the concrete number to cite when arguing open-model substitution in security workloads.
insights.quote: Five of the 11 open detections (45%) detected at least one attack, compared with 10 frontier detections (29%).

insights.claim: After the independent quality review, three open-pipeline detections qualified as gold and covered all eight attacks, while no frontier detections qualified as gold at all.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: Full attack coverage from three artifacts suggests high-quality behavioral detections consolidate coverage — a small number of good rules can displace a large rule estate, which matters for SIEM/detection-engine cost models.
insights.quote: After review, three open detections and no frontier detections qualified as gold. The three open detections still covered all eight attacks.

insights.claim: Qualifying as gold required not just firing on attacks but also remaining quiet on available test traffic and passing an independent review for behavioral grounding, multiple signals, and absence of environment-specific strings.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: A concrete multi-gate rubric buyers can impose on any agentic security vendor; ask for gold-equivalent numbers, not detection counts.
insights.quote: To qualify as gold, detections also had to remain quiet on available test traffic and pass an independent review for behavioral grounding, multiple signals, and no environment-specific strings.
insights.locator: Detection alone, however, was only the first quality gate.

insights.claim: Every passing detection was deployed verbatim to the live detection engine and an independent third-party model judged whether each match represented the intended attack behavior, removing human cherry-picking from the results.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: Verbatim deployment plus third-party judging is a credibility standard worth demanding; most vendor benchmarks lack both.
insights.quote: Every passing detection was deployed verbatim to the live detection engine.
insights.locator: Evaluating the complete agent system from backtest to live fire

insights.claim: The authors explicitly scope the work as a directional system-level case study rather than a general benchmark, noting it covered one scenario family with small detection sets so cross-scenario generalization remains untested.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: Discount headline open-vs-frontier claims accordingly; the result is a directional signal for procurement conversations, not proof of general model substitution.
insights.quote: The findings are a directional system-level case study, not a general benchmark.

insights.claim: Limited benign traffic in the test environment means the noise test does not represent production false-positive performance, and three of eight live-fire runs experienced harness failures yet were retained because they produced complete telemetry.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: False positives are the real operating cost in security operations and remain unmeasured here; a 37.5% harness failure rate also signals agentic reliability is not yet production-grade.
insights.quote: Three of eight live-fire runs experienced harness failures but produced complete telemetry and were retained.

insights.claim: Because the optimized configuration changed both the harness and the model stack simultaneously, the reported gain reflects the entire pipeline and cannot be attributed to the model in an isolated ablation.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: Do not read the 2.5x as a model-quality result; it is a system result, which weakens any narrative that Nemotron weights alone substitute for frontier models.
insights.quote: Because the optimized configuration changed both the harness and model stack, the gain reflects the complete open pipeline rather than an isolated model ablation.

insights.claim: The four design principles offered for specialized agents are: define measurable tasks with clear per-model responsibilities, post-train with domain data and verifiable rewards, ground outputs in authoritative context validated by deterministic checks and realistic replay, and evaluate the complete workflow in realistic conditions with experts controlling guardrails.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: A portable checklist for judging any vertical agent startup — those missing verifiable rewards or execution-based validation are likely to underdeliver in production.
insights.locator: Applying the pattern to specialized agents

insights.claim: CrowdStrike is productizing this offense-defense coevolution loop as SafeMind, its agentic cybersecurity system, with NVIDIA Nemotron models customized for cybersecurity operating inside it.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: A named product tie-up between a top endpoint vendor and NVIDIA's open model line — track SafeMind commercialization as the read-through for whether agentic security converts to revenue.
insights.quote: CrowdStrike is advancing this approach through SafeMind, its agentic cybersecurity system, which brings offensive and defensive AI together in a continuous coevolution loop.

insights.claim: The Open Secure AI Alliance is cited as expanding the broader ecosystem of open models, harnesses, and tools for cybersecurity, indicating an organized industry push to standardize open agentic security tooling.
insights.speaker: Roberto Rodriguez
insights.so_what: Consortium formation typically precedes commoditization of the harness layer; watch whether standardization erodes the differentiation vendors are currently building there.
